Sub-Reality describes a condition of the image; Sub-Realism must assert an obligation.

the referent was not liquidated but impounded

An actual property of the recording: the surplus of the record over the intention and over the narrative economy that contains it.
Sub-reality — the mode of access under which a seal becomes readable from a later space-time. Not in the film. Not in the spectator.
A reading is admissible when it is anchored in a determinate trace, doubly dated, bearing a named counter-narrative, and actualised as a work. These are norms, not proofs.
Censorship apparatuses are language-shaped. They read scripts, titles, dialogue, synopses, denunciations, and they read them reliably.
I have not checked a single archive. It is plausible, it is central, and it is currently unsupported

the first image form in which the seal is a measurable quantity
proposition 5 is an empirical claim that no one has checked, and proposition 11 is a formal promise you have not yet kept in a work.
The document labels all four repairs VIRTUAL–INFERRED and as the preparer's own constructions, not Karyağdı's; the Part IX proposal and the printed 'entry' (line 64) carry the same label.
The document marks as OPEN–UNVERIFIED whether any Part IX or 2000–2030 successor volume is in preparation; it worked from the 2003 New Edition structure.

My reading: Repair 1 keeps the Institute's distinction intact by making 'seal' the material term, 'sub-reality' the theoretical access-relation, and 'Sub-Realism' the practice (sealing + lectorship). The text does not state this three-way mapping in one sentence.

My reading: 4a and 4c pull against each other. 4a treats the seal as recorded-but-unseen (a quantity of attention); line 39 and 4c treat it as surplus over the maker's intention. Unseen area and unintended content are not the same thing.
Open conjecture (mine): in a 360° recording, the portion no viewer visits contains content that passes the 'anchored' test, i.e. the unseen is not merely empty sky/floor. Untested.

Open conjecture (the text's own, flagged unverified at line 86): censorship interventions cluster at language-bearing stages (script, title, synopsis) rather than at duration/framing; the ratio is checkable in archives but unchecked.

The packet omits the tables (README line 2), including the 'Placement against the 1900–2000 structure' table (line 23) and the proposed Part IX section list (IX.26, IX.27 are referenced but never defined). Can you supply them?

The MA thesis (2021), Babelsberg appendix (2022), the Sub-realism / Sub-reality paper and the 19 July 2026 terminology lock are cited but not in the packet. Can you supply them so that quotations attributed to them (e.g. line 36) can be checked at source?
Who prepared this document (the 'I' of the text)? The packet names only the addressee, and the twelve propositions are drafted by the preparer in your name. Do you endorse them as your own position?

# Production plan — Örnek Restoran tanıtım filmi (sentetik brif)

Plan tarihi: 2026-11-17 (Salı). Teslime 17 takvim günü, çekimden teslime 10 takvim günü var.
Bu bir taslaktır; insan incelemesi içindir.

## Inputs read

- `brief.md`
- `tasks.csv`

## Constraints and dates

| Kısıt / tarih | Kaynak |
|---|---|
| Kapsam: 60 saniyelik tanıtım filmi + 3 adet 9:16 Reels kesimi | brief.md:4 |
| Çekim: tek gün, tek mekân (restoran salonu ve mutfak), 2026-11-24 (Salı) | brief.md:5 |
| Teslim: 2026-12-04 (Cuma), saat 12:00 | brief.md:6 |

- **1. revizyon turu kaba kurgu üzerinden yapılır.** Tam bitmiş paket ilk tura gönderilirse iki tur × 2 iş günü bekleme ile takvimde hiç boşluk kalmıyor; kaba kurguyu 2026-11-25'te göndermek 2026-12-04 sabahını yedek olarak bırakıyor.

# Claim-evidence map — Sub-Realism, Part IX

Source: `sub-realism-part-ix.txt` (document prepared for M. Ozan Karyağdı, Berlin, 25 August 2026; plain-text extraction, tables omitted).

**Who is speaking.** The document is written by an unnamed preparer addressing Karyağdı. It says the Part IX proposal, the four repairs and the printed "entry" are the preparer's constructions (lines 12, 34, 64). The claims below are therefore the document's claims, not Karyağdı's own, unless he adopts them.

**Terms as used here.** *Sub-reality* is the theoretical concept (a mode of access). *Sub-Realism* is the artistic practice/movement. *Seal* is the document's proposed term for the material property of a recording.

## Claims

"Status" is my classification of how the claim relates to the text. "Document's own label" is the status the text gives itself.

| # | Claim | Located passage (file:line) | Status | Document's own label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *Art in Theory* admits positions, not descriptions. Sub-reality began as an analytic category, so Sub-Realism must be converted into a position with a named antagonist and a practice. | `sub-realism-part-ix.txt:15` "an idea enters not by being true but by being legible as a refusal of something else that was current at the time"; `:17` "Sub-Reality describes a condition of the image; Sub-Realism must assert an obligation." | stated | Line 15 ACTUAL–VERIFIED; the scoring at line 20 VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 2 | The antagonist is Baudrillard's simulacrum thesis: the referent was impounded, not liquidated, and can become readable later. | `:25` "the referent was not liquidated but impounded"; `:25` "Hyperreality is a claim about circulation; sub-reality is a claim about the deposit." | stated | VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 3 | Sub-Realism belongs with realism, not Surrealism. The prefix marks deferred legibility, not a lower layer, so the dream/memory vertical scheme should be demoted. | `:28` "sub- marks not a lower layer but a deferred legibility." | stated | VIRTUAL–INFERRED; the demotion is OPEN–UNVERIFIED (line 88) |
| 4 | Repair 1: the seal is an actual, material property of the recording; sub-reality is not in the film but is the mode of access from a later space-time. | `:39` "An actual property of the recording: the surplus of the record over the intention and over the narrative economy that contains it."; `:40` "Sub-reality — the mode of access under which a seal becomes readable from a later space-time. Not in the film. Not in the spectator." | stated | VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 5 | Repair 2: lectorship is governed by four admissibility norms (anchored, doubly dated, counter-narrative-bearing, actualised), not by a truth condition. | `:78` "A reading is admissible when it is anchored in a determinate trace, doubly dated, bearing a named counter-narrative, and actualised as a work. These are norms, not proofs." | stated | VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 6 | Repair 3 / proposition 5: censorship apparatuses read language reliably and read duration, framing and surplus unreliably and late. This is offered as the empirical core. | `:54` "Censorship apparatuses are language-shaped. They read scripts, titles, dialogue, synopses, denunciations, and they read them reliably."; `:86` "I have not checked a single archive. It is plausible, it is central, and it is currently unsupported" | hypothesis (the text's own, unchecked) | OPEN–UNVERIFIED |
| 7 | Repair 4c: a generated image bears no seal, because nothing was recorded. This turns "anti-simulacra" into a technical specification. | `:62` "A generated image has no seal. There is no surplus, because nothing was recorded" | stated | VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 8 | Repair 4a / proposition 11: the 360° recording is Sub-Realism's native form, because the seal becomes a measurable quantity (recorded but unseen). | `:60` "the first image form in which the seal is a measurable quantity"; `:84` "proposition 5 is an empirical claim that no one has checked, and proposition 11 is a formal promise you have not yet kept in a work." | stated; not yet realised in a work | VIRTUAL–INFERRED |
| 9 | The seal / sub-reality / Sub-Realism split maps onto material property / theoretical concept / practice. | `:36-41` (no single sentence states this) | interpreted (my reading) | — |
| 10 | 4a and 4c use two different notions of the seal: "unseen by the viewer" versus "unintended by the maker". | `:39`, `:60`, `:62` | interpreted (my reading) | — |
| 11 | In a 360° recording, the portion no viewer visits contains anchorable content rather than only empty sky or floor. | `:60` (conjecture drawn from it) | hypothesis (mine) | — |

## Counterarguments and uncertainty

The text names its own two most load-bearing claims at line 84: proposition 5 (claim 6) and proposition 11 (claim 8). I follow that.

**Claim 6: censorship is language-shaped.**

- **Strongest objection.** Censors also acted on finished images. Post-production cuts, shelving of completed films, and objections to visual tone or style would all be cases of an apparatus reading the non-verbal, and reading it in time. If such interventions are common, the claim that the "machinery that polices the sayable therefore passes over" the image (line 76) fails. This objection is mine; the packet neither raises nor answers it.
- **Measurement problem.** A high share of script-stage interventions may reflect only that scripts are reviewed first and are cheaper to change. It would not show that images are illegible to censors.
- **The prediction is loose.** "If the ratio is what you expect" (line 55) gives no threshold, so as written it cannot fail.
- **Where the text marks it unverified.** Line 86 is OPEN–UNVERIFIED: no archive was checked. Line 84 says no one has checked it. Line 55 describes it as checkable, not checked.

**Claim 8: 360° as native form, the seal as a quantity.**

- **Strongest objection.** The seal is defined at line 39 as surplus over the maker's intention. Line 60 measures something else: what a viewer did not look at. A fully staged 360° scene would have a large unseen fraction and no unintended surplus. The "quantity" may therefore measure viewer attention and not the seal (my interpretation, claim 10).
- **Second objection.** The text itself states that total givenness looks like "the least sub-realist format imaginable" (line 59). Its reply relies on redistributing the out-of-field to attention, which is asserted, not demonstrated.
- **Where the text marks it unverified.** Line 84 calls proposition 11 "a formal promise you have not yet kept in a work." The whole of Repair 4 is VIRTUAL–INFERRED (line 34).

**Other uncertainty the text flags.**

- Whether a Part IX or a 2000–2030 successor volume exists or is in preparation is OPEN–UNVERIFIED (line 87). Claim 1's framing of a "gap" depends on it.
- The admissibility tests are "a set of disciplinary norms, not a verification procedure in the scientific sense" (line 49).
- The demotion of the vertical scheme awaits Karyağdı's decision (line 88).
- The status of the deferred *Mirror* article is unresolved (line 89).

## Experiment proposal

Tests hypothesis 11, and with it claim 8. I chose this over the archival test of claim 6 because it can be bounded with material the packet says already exists (cinematic VR practice, line 58). The archival test needs sources whose availability the packet does not establish.

- **Question.** In a 360° recording, is the recorded-but-unvisited portion a seal in the sense of line 39 (unintended, anchorable surplus), or is it only unattended area?
- **Material.**
  - One short, already-shot, unstaged 360° recording of a few minutes.
  - A headset that logs head orientation.
  - A small group of viewers.
  - The maker's written statement, made before any viewing, of what they intended the piece to record.
- **Procedure.**
  1. The maker writes the statement of intention and it is set aside.
  2. Each viewer watches once. Orientation is logged.
  3. Compute per-viewer coverage (share of the sphere-time seen) and the union across all viewers.
  4. Two readers who did not make the piece inspect only the region no viewer visited. They list every determinate trace that meets the "anchored" test (line 45) and is absent from the maker's statement.
  5. As a control, they do the same for the most-visited region.
  6. Exhibit the coverage map and the two lists as the work, which satisfies the "actualised" test (line 48).
- **What would count against it.**
  - The union of viewers covers nearly all of the sphere-time, so nothing meaningful stays unvisited.
  - The unvisited region yields no anchorable traces, only sky, floor or the rig.
